discovery: Controlled/living radical polymerization (atom transfer radical polymerization, ATRP), enabling precise synthesis of well-defined polymers and functional macromolecular materials
rationale: Recent prizes have covered protein design (2024) and metal-organic frameworks (2025), so a turn back to synthetic and polymer chemistry is plausible. ATRP, discovered independently in 1995 by Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto, is among the most cited breakthroughs in modern chemistry. It changed how precisely polymers can be made and is used widely in industry, and both scientists have received many major awards (Wolf Prize, Dreyfus Prize, among others) that often come before a Nobel.
